critical_evidence.evidence: Cylinder bores were borescoped in August 2026 by the seller's local independent Porsche mechanic, who reported all cylinders 'in excellent condition.' Scope images are in the listing gallery (seller cites photos 291-296) with the shop's service record at photo 369. Those specific images were not in the set captured here, and the report as quoted does not break out cylinders 4-6 individually or state whether it was a cold or warm scope.

Seller states his mechanic pulled a DME report and posted the ignition readings (photo 363), inviting the community to interpret them. The over-rev range 1-6 table and its mileage stamps are not quoted in the text, and the page was not in the captured photo set, so the actual over-rev counts remain unestablished.

Dated work is described: water pump, thermostat, drive belt and coolant May 2024; rear main seal Sept 2019 with TuneRS direct oil feed IMS flange; spark plugs Aug 2026; engine-mount insert and oil change Nov 2025. Carfax shows 22 service entries and records accompany the car, but the invoices themselves were not examined here and there is no AOS replacement or test, and no mention of the plastic coolant-pipe/expansion-tank condition.

documentation.rationale: VIN, original window sticker, owner's manual, clean Carfax with 22 service entries, dated service history spanning 2019-2026, an independent Porsche shop's August 2026 borescope with retained images and an invoice, a DME report page, and multiple seller-shot cold-start and driving videos. Short of a 9-10 only because the borescope and DME pages were not in the captured set for direct reading, the mechanic's written report is quoted rather than reproduced, and there is no AOS or pre-2019 maintenance trail.

condition.rationale: Specific evidence rather than prose: brand-new Continental ExtremeContact Sport 02 tires (Aug 2026, replacing 2018 date codes), spark plugs Aug 2026, water pump/thermostat/belt/coolant May 2024, rear main seal 2019, IMS direct oil feed, borescope reported excellent, 38k miles, garaged, never tracked. Paint looks deep and straight in the photos with disclosed hood chips and a faint mark above the driver's door handle; the underbody photo shows only normal surface rust on exhaust parts. Clutch, AOS and suspension condition remain untested, which keeps it below 9.

price_value.rationale: Current bid of $25,000 sits below the deterministic fair-value band of $28,863-$33,986 (mid $29,988) for mileage-adjusted 2006-2008 S comps, and this car carries a fresh borescope, new tires and recent cooling work that most comps lack. It is a live auction with 674 watchers and three days to run, so the bid is a floor, not the price; at the mid of fair value the value case is average rather than a bargain, and no known-work deductions apply.

mission_fit.rationale: A 987.1 Cayman S manual is explicitly a keeper choice in the profile, and the S is permitted only with unusually strong engine due diligence, which the August 2026 specialist borescope plus DME report largely supplies. It does not solve the accelerated-bridge problem, and the profile's more comfortable bore-scoring choice is the 2.7; spending near the middle of the budget band on a keeper conflicts with cash preservation while the 335i is out of service.

logistics.rationale: York, Pennsylvania is a cross-country buy and the sale is a binding BaT auction closing 9/24 at roughly 7:47am Pacific, so any pre-purchase inspection must be arranged with the seller in the next two days or money moves without one. Offsetting this: the seller is highly responsive, has posted cold-start and drive videos, a recent independent-shop inspection exists, and a stock 2008 Cayman S is straightforward to register and smog in California; BaT shipping is available and the car is drivable home.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Six-speed manual Cayman S with only 38k miles, Preferred Package Plus, bi-xenons, heated seats, Bose and the deployable spoiler, plus a documented borescope and preventive IMS oil feed. Black over black is the most common and least distinctive combination, and the Numeric cables give a notchier-than-factory shift, so it is a desirable but not rare specification.

ppi_focus: Independent re-verification or review of the August 2026 borescope images, with attention to cylinders 4-6 and the wrist-pin/scoring signature typical of the M97
Full DME readout on the shop's PIWIS: over-rev ranges, stored fault memory, adaptation values
AOS vacuum test and inspection of the oil filler for emulsion or smoke at idle after a hot restart
Plastic coolant pipes, expansion tank seams, radiators and condensers for weeping and debris damage; verify the 2024 water pump job's workmanship
Clutch engagement point, dual-mass flywheel rattle at idle, and confirmation that the Numeric shift cables were routed and secured correctly
Rear main seal area and transaxle bellhousing for fresh oil after the 2019 repair
Front and rear suspension bushings, control arms, drop links and shock condition — original at 18 years
Lift inspection of the floor pan, jack points and subframe for East Coast corrosion beyond the exhaust surface rust visible in photos
Paint-depth readings across all panels, especially the driver's door and the PPF-covered front bumper and arches
Brake rotor thickness and crack check on the cross-drilled discs, plus brake fluid moisture test
what_would_change_verdict: A full DME over-rev printout showing no range 4-6 events, plus a written cylinder-by-cylinder borescope report naming 4, 5 and 6, would close the profile's hard engine gate outright
An independent Porsche-specialist PPI arranged near York before the 9/24 close (or a seller willing to hold the sale for one) would resolve the binding-bid exposure
Documented AOS replacement or a passing vacuum test, plus confirmation of clutch health, would remove the two largest remaining open costs
A hammer well above the fair-value band, or discovery of undisclosed paint/bodywork near the door-handle blemish, would erode the value case
Evidence that the IMS oil feed flange was installed without a proper invoice or by a non-specialist would reopen engine risk despite the clean scope
evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper this is close to the profile's ideal shape for an S: a manual 987.1 3.4 with a recent specialist borescope, a DME report offered, fresh tires and preventive cooling work — the only terms on which the profile permits a Cayman S at all. It does nothing for the accelerated-bridge problem and would consume the middle of the budget band while the 335i sits unsold, so it competes directly with the cash-preservation strategy rather than complementing it.
evidence.rationale: This listing establishes more engine-specific evidence than most 987.1 S cars: an independent Porsche mechanic borescoped the bores in August 2026 with images in the gallery and the invoice photographed, a DME report was pulled and its ignition page posted, and dated invoicing exists for the May 2024 water pump/thermostat/coolant service, the 2019 rear main seal and TuneRS IMS oil feed flange, November 2025 engine mount and oil change, and August 2026 spark plugs. Carfax shows no reported accidents, 22 service entries, three previous owners including a corporate fleet, and a last reported reading of 36,221 miles against 38k indicated — an earlier reading, not an inconsistency. Tires are new Continental ExtremeContact Sport 02s fitted August 2026 specifically because the previous set was 2018 date-coded, so the usual low-mileage tire liability is already retired. Observed negatives are limited and self-disclosed: the factory shift cables snapped in November 2025 and were replaced with Numeric Racing cables, hood chips, a chip on a roof-rack-mount cover, and a faint mark above the driver's door handle. What remains open is the over-rev range data itself (only ignition readings are referenced), any AOS service or test in 18 years, clutch and flywheel condition, plastic coolant pipe condition, and the pre-2019 history. Photos show straight black paint, an unworn-looking black leather interior, a stock engine bay and an underside with normal surface rust on exhaust components only. The bid of $25,000 sits below the $28,863-$33,986 mileage-adjusted fair-value band with three days and 674 watchers remaining, and the sale is a binding online auction in York, Pennsylvania closing roughly 7:47am Pacific on 9/24, so no independent inspection is currently scheduled ahead of commitment.
